title: Recover an adder tree from a flattened netlist
objective: Analyze a flattened, gate-level Verilog netlist over four 16-bit input buses (a, b, c, d) and a single 32-bit output (sum), and produce a clean, synthesizable, word-level Verilog RTL module that is behaviorally (I/O) equivalent to the reference netlist for every input combination.
expected_output_summary: A single self-contained Verilog file at submission/recovered_rtl.v defining module recovered_design(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input [15:0] c, input [15:0] d, output [31:0] sum) implementing word-level combinational RTL that reproduces the reference netlist's behavior bit-for-bit across randomized and corner-case test vectors, without merely wrapping or copying the provided netlist/primitive cells.

metrics.name: word_recovery_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of required word-level functional behavior correctly reproduced across the full randomized+corner-case test vector suite; computed as (# vectors matching)/(# vectors applied).

metrics.name: structural_match_accuracy
metrics.description: Binary/graded score indicating whether the submission passes the structural non-recovery gate (i.e. is genuinely word-level recovered RTL rather than a disguised copy of the flattened netlist or a wrapper around its primitives).

metrics.name: functional_equivalence
metrics.description: Overall PASS/FAIL verdict: 1 if 100% of test vectors match between recovered_design and the reference flattened netlist AND compilation succeeds AND the structural gate passes; 0 otherwise.
